title: Build it: the library’s book tools
summary: Small functions that each do one job, with a docstring saying what and type hints saying what goes in and out, add up to a tool: format_book, search with a default field, and report, which sorts what search finds with a lambda key. A short program on top asks what to look for.
objectives: Split a job into small functions that each do one thing.
Use defaults and key= in a real tool.
Test each function on its own, then together.

slides.say: Meera wants to type “narayan” and see every R. K. Narayan book, oldest first, one tidy line each. Three small functions do it: one formats, one finds, one reports.
p: Meera wants to type “narayan” and see every R. K. Narayan book, oldest first, one tidy line each. Three small functions do it: one formats, one finds, one reports.

visual.text:
books = [
    {"title": "Wings of Fire", "author": "A. P. J. Abdul Kalam", "year": 1999, "copies": 3},
    {"title": "The Guide", "author": "R. K. Narayan", "year": 1958, "copies": 2},
    {"title": "Malgudi Days", "author": "R. K. Narayan", "year": 1943, "copies": 4},
    {"title": "Godan", "author": "Premchand", "year": 1936, "copies": 1},
    {"title": "The God of Small Things", "author": "Arundhati Roy", "year": 1997, "copies": 1},
    {"title": "Swami and Friends", "author": "R. K. Narayan", "year": 1935, "copies": 2},
]


def format_book(book: dict) -> str:
    """One line for a book: title, author and year."""
    return f"{book['title']} by {book['author']} ({book['year']})"


def search(books: list, text: str, field: str = "title") -> list:
    """The books whose field contains text, ignoring capitals."""
    found = []
    for b in books:
        if text.lower() in b[field].lower():
            found.append(b)
    return found


def report(books: list, text: str, field: str = "title") -> None:
    """Print the books that match, oldest first."""
    found = sorted(search(books, text, field), key=lambda b: b["year"])
    print(f'{len(found)} found for "{text}" in {field}')
    for b in found:
        print("-", format_book(b))


report(books, "narayan", "author")
visual.out:
3 found for "narayan" in author
- Swami and Friends by R. K. Narayan (1935)
- Malgudi Days by R. K. Narayan (1943)
- The Guide by R. K. Narayan (1958)

slides.say: A **docstring** is the text in quotes on the first line of a function: it says what the function does. **Type hints** say what each parameter and the result should be. Python doesn’t enforce them; people and editors read them.
points: `def search(books: list, text: str, field: str = "title") -> list:`
`-> None` means it returns nothing useful.

def fine(days: int, rate: int = 2) -> int:
